detected_issues.value: 0.39 x leg length ahead of hip
detected_issues.recommendation: The foot is landing ~39% of a leg length ahead of the hip at contact with a heel strike. This brakes each step and raises impact load. Increasing cadence toward 170-190 spm and landing with the foot closer under the hip reduces overstride.

analysis_confidence.explanation: Pose tracking occasionally confused the left and right legs; leg-based metrics may be less precise. Try a clearer video with the whole body in frame, or film from a different angle.

capture_report.headline: This is almost always a symptom of how few pixels of you there were (the row above) rather than a fault of its own. If that was fine, the other two causes are a body reading as a dark silhouette -- keep the light behind the camera, not behind the athlete -- and a view almost exactly side-on, where a few degrees of angle helps separate the legs.

issues.label: Cadence
issues.instruction: Run in place with high knee lift 3x30 seconds. Use a metronome app set to 180 bpm.
issues.cue: Imagine running on hot coals -- quick, light steps

issues.label: Overstride
issues.problem: Overstriding -- foot lands 0.4x leg length ahead of the hip (optimal under 0.15)
issues.instruction: Run 4x20 seconds at a deliberately higher step rate on a metronome set to 180 bpm, focusing on landing with the foot under your hips rather than reaching out in front.
issues.cue: Land under your body, not out in front -- shorter, quicker steps

issues.label: Elbow Angle
issues.problem: Elbow angle too wide (114.0 deg, optimal 85-100 deg)
issues.instruction: Standing, practice pendulum arm swing with elbows at 90 deg. 3x30 seconds, then transfer to running.
issues.cue: Hold a crisp in your fist without breaking it -- soft hands, sharp angle

issues.label: Foot Strike
issues.problem: Heel-first foot-strike, which usually pairs with overstriding and a braking force at contact
issues.instruction: Run 4x20 seconds barefoot on grass or in minimal shoes, letting the midfoot/forefoot make first contact. Keep steps short and quick; do not force a hard toe-strike.
issues.cue: Land softly on the middle of your foot, under your hips
